article_title: AIED's Unfinished Mission: Centering Agency and Motivation in the Age of Effortless Bypass
citation: H. Chad Lane. (2026). AIED's Unfinished Mission: Centering Agency and Motivation in the Age of Effortless Bypass. AIED 2026, CCIS 3032, pp. 502–516. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-29791-4_38
title: Bypass-aware tutor: detects bypass engagement patterns and responds with adaptive metacognitive scaffolding rather than restriction
description: A bypass-aware tutor extends Baker's gaming-the-system detection paradigm to the GenAI era: rather than preventing bypass through restriction, which SDT predicts will produce backlash, the envisioned system detects engagement patterns such as sudden jumps in solution quality, large text pastes, and surface-level interaction, and responds with adaptive metacognitive scaffolding, prompting learners to explain reasoning or attempt a similar problem inside the tutor.
requirements: Research is needed on interaction patterns that reliably distinguish productive AI use from bypass; tone must be diagnostic, not accusatory
constraints: The paper states purely technical bypass detection is an arms race AIED cannot win on its own, since determined students can retype LLM steps with plausible pacing
target_learners: Learners using AI tools who may attempt bypass
target_learning_goals: Metacognitive resilience; accurate self-assessment calibration; internalized self-regulatory habits
examples: The paper envisions a longitudinal profile visible to the learner in the open learner model tradition, displaying when they engaged deeply versus offloaded and how unassisted performance compares to assisted work
key_sources: H. Chad Lane. (2026). AIED's Unfinished Mission: Centering Agency and Motivation in the Age of Effortless Bypass. AIED 2026, CCIS 3032, pp. 502–516. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-29791-4_38

article_title: Memdora: Designing Cognitively-Grounded Flashcard Interactions for AI-Powered Spaced Repetition
citation: Ruiyang Zhang. (2027). Memdora: Designing Cognitively-Grounded Flashcard Interactions for AI-Powered Spaced Repetition. Proceedings of ACM International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces (IUI '27). https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25096
title: By Heart single card type with three self-selectable retrieval modes of varying difficulty
description: For verbatim memorization of extended passages, By Heart presents one card type with three user-selectable retrieval modes: Strip Peek (all lines hidden, tap to reveal for 2 seconds, highest effort), Step Through (past lines dimmed, current line bold), and First Word (opening word only as cue, lowest effort). The modes are "three points on the cue-target continuum identified in retrieval practice research", and self-selection per session operationalizes desirable difficulties within a practical UI.
requirements: Displaying all three options simultaneously so the difficulty spectrum is explicit, supporting learner agency over difficulty selection
constraints: Claimed as the first SRS system to operationalize self-selected difficulty for extended passage memorization, to the authors' knowledge
target_learners: learners memorizing poems, scripts, or extended passages verbatim
examples: The three modes are demonstrated on the same poem (Dylan Thomas, The Force That Through the Green Fuse), with difficulty increasing from First Word to Strip Peek
key_sources: Ruiyang Zhang. (2027). Memdora: Designing Cognitively-Grounded Flashcard Interactions for AI-Powered Spaced Repetition. Proceedings of ACM International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces (IUI '27). https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25096

article_title: A Randomized Controlled Study Evaluating a Brief, Bystander Bullying Intervention with Junior High School Students
citation: Midgett, A., Doumas, D., Trull, R., & Johnston, A. (2016). A Randomized Controlled Study Evaluating a Brief, Bystander Bullying Intervention with Junior High School Students. Boise State University. https://eric.ed.gov/?q=A+Randomized+Controlled+Study+Evaluating+a+Brief+Bystander+Bullying+Intervention
title: Four bystander roles in bullying situations
description: The article organizes student bystander responses into four roles drawn from Salmivalli et al. (1996): "(a) assistants who actively and directly help the bully victimize a target, (b) reinforcers who laugh at or simply witness the situation, (c) outsiders who often disengage or walk away from the group, and (d) defenders who intervene and/or console the target of bullying." This taxonomy motivates the STAC program's aim of moving bystanders into the defender role, since passive bystanders report guilt and moral disengagement while defenders report increased confidence and decreased anxiety.
requirements: Bystanders must be able to recognize bullying situations to classify responses into the four roles
constraints: The taxonomy is attributed to Salmivalli et al. (1996) as background theory, not tested in this study
target_learners: junior high school students who witness bullying
target_learning_goals: recognize bystander roles and adopt the defender role when witnessing bullying
examples: The STAC program trains selected student leaders to move from reinforcer or outsider roles into the defender role by using the four STAC strategies
key_sources: Midgett, A., Doumas, D., Trull, R., & Johnston, A. (2016). A Randomized Controlled Study Evaluating a Brief, Bystander Bullying Intervention with Junior High School Students. Boise State University. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1146195

article_title: A mixed method study on Chinese primary school EFL teachers' preparation, affecting factors and support needed to implement intercultural foreign language teaching.
citation: Wang Huang, Xu Tianyuan, Zhang Mengxue. (2023). A mixed method study on Chinese primary school EFL teachers’ preparation, affecting factors and support needed to implement intercultural foreign language teaching. PLOS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0284146
title: Byram's model of intercultural communicative competence as the study's theoretical framework
description: The study adopts Byram's model, in which intercultural communicative competence comprises linguistic, sociolinguistic, discourse and intercultural competence, the last including attitudes, knowledge, skills of interpreting/relating, skills of discovering/interaction, and critical cultural awareness. The article states it "aims to produce intercultural speakers instead of native-like speakers" while highlighting foreign language proficiency, which made it "one of the most highly cited, widely tested, and practiced models" and the framework of this study.
requirements: Teachers must themselves become intercultural competent and be prepared for the demands of intercultural foreign language teaching
target_learners: primary school EFL pupils in China
target_learning_goals: intercultural competence, including cultural awareness, attitudes, knowledge and skills
examples: The questionnaire design refers to Sercu and Bandura's instrument and was shaped for primary school EFL teachers in the Chinese context, using Byram's model as the theoretical framework
key_sources: Wang Huang, Xu Tianyuan, Zhang Mengxue. (2023). A mixed method study on Chinese primary school EFL teachers’ preparation, affecting factors and support needed to implement intercultural foreign language teaching. PLOS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0284146
